paragraphs.title: Zedekiah’s Rebellion and the Siege of Jerusalem

easy.explanation: Verse 1 says Zedekiah was one and twenty years old when he began to reign.
easy.q: How old was Zedekiah when he began to reign?

easy.explanation: Zedekiah reigned eleven years in Jerusalem.
easy.q: How many years did Zedekiah reign in Jerusalem?

easy.explanation: Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon came against Jerusalem with all his army.
easy.q: Who came against Jerusalem with his army?

answers: Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon
medium.explanation: The passage says that Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.
medium.q: Why did the siege of Jerusalem take place?

medium.explanation: The famine was sore in the city, and there was no bread for the people.
medium.q: What happened as the siege continued?

medium.explanation: Nebuchadrezzar’s army pitched against Jerusalem and built forts around it.
medium.q: What did the Babylonians build against Jerusalem?

challenge.explanation: The siege continued until the eleventh year, when famine and the city’s fall occurred.
challenge.q: What does the siege lasting unto Zedekiah’s eleventh year show?

answers: After the city was broken up
challenge.explanation: The men of war fled after the city was broken up and the Chaldeans surrounded it.
challenge.q: When did the men of war flee from Jerusalem?

answers: By the way of the plain
challenge.explanation: They went by the way of the plain.
challenge.q: By what way did the fugitives leave Jerusalem?

paragraphs.title: The Capture and Punishment of Zedekiah

easy.explanation: The army of the Chaldeans overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho.
easy.q: Where did the Chaldeans overtake Zedekiah?

easy.explanation: Zedekiah was carried to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
The king of Babylon slew the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes.
easy.q: What did the king of Babylon do to Zedekiah’s sons?

medium.explanation: All his army was scattered from him.
His eyes were put out, he was bound in chains, and he was put in prison.
medium.q: What was the sequence of Zedekiah’s punishments?

answers: He sent him back to Jerusalem
medium.explanation: The expression means that the king pronounced judgment upon Zedekiah.
medium.q: What does it mean that the king of Babylon “gave judgment upon him”?

answers: His eyes had been put out
challenge.explanation: The passage says that Zedekiah’s eyes were put out before he was carried to Babylon.
challenge.q: Why could Zedekiah not see Babylon, where he was taken?

answers: His army was scattered before he was captured
challenge.explanation: His army was scattered, and then he was taken by the Chaldeans.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage show between Zedekiah’s capture and his army?

answers: He was judged immediately in Jerusalem
He was brought to Babylon’s ruling center
challenge.explanation: He was taken to Riblah and brought before the king of Babylon for judgment.
challenge.q: What does Zedekiah’s being taken to Riblah indicate?

paragraphs.title: The Destruction of Jerusalem and the Deportation

answers: The house of the LORD, the king’s house, and the houses of Jerusalem
easy.explanation: Nebuzar-adan burned the house of the LORD, the king’s house, and the houses of Jerusalem.
easy.q: What did Nebuzar-adan burn in Jerusalem?

easy.explanation: The army of the Chaldeans broke down all the walls of Jerusalem.
easy.q: What did the Chaldeans do to Jerusalem’s walls?

answers: Some of the poor, including vinedressers and husbandmen
easy.explanation: He left certain of the poor of the land for vinedressers and husbandmen.
easy.q: Whom did Nebuzar-adan leave in the land?

answers: They were all restored to Jerusalem
medium.explanation: The passage says that Judah was carried away captive out of its own land.
medium.q: What happened to the people after the city was destroyed?

answers: The poor, the remaining people, those who submitted, and the multitude
medium.explanation: Verse 15 lists several groups of people who were carried away captive.
medium.q: Which groups were carried away captive?

medium.explanation: Husbandmen were people who worked the land.

answers: Some people remained to work the land
challenge.explanation: Farmers were left so that the land could continue to be cultivated.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from leaving vinedressers and husbandmen in the land?

answers: Burning, breaking down the walls, and deportation
challenge.explanation: The passage first describes the burning, then the broken walls, and then the people carried away.
challenge.q: What order of events is presented?

challenge.explanation: The wording emphasizes that the destruction affected much of Jerusalem.
challenge.q: What does the repeated description of all the houses and walls emphasize?

paragraphs.title: The Plundering of the Temple Vessels

easy.explanation: They carried all the brass of the vessels to Babylon.
easy.q: Where did the Chaldeans carry the brass vessels?

answers: The pillars and the brasen sea
easy.explanation: The passage mentions the pillars and the brasen sea.
easy.q: Which Temple objects are specifically mentioned?

easy.explanation: These objects are repeatedly described as being made of brass.
easy.q: What were the pillars, the sea, and the bulls made of?

answers: They broke them and carried away the brass
They left them in the Temple
medium.explanation: They broke the vessels and carried their brass to Babylon.
medium.q: What did the Chaldeans do to the Temple pillars, bases, and sea?

medium.explanation: The passage describes brass vessels and also vessels of gold and silver.
medium.q: Which materials are mentioned among the Temple vessels?

answers: The upper part of a pillar
medium.explanation: A chapiter was the decorated upper part of a pillar.

challenge.explanation: The detailed list shows how thoroughly the Temple furnishings were taken away.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the many details about the Temple vessels?

challenge.explanation: The passage mentions two pillars and twelve brasen bulls.
challenge.q: How many pillars and brass bulls are mentioned?

answers: Ninety-six were on a side, and one hundred were around the network
challenge.explanation: Verse 23 records ninety-six on a side and one hundred around the network.
challenge.q: What detail about the pomegranates could easily be missed?

paragraphs.title: The Capture of Judah’s Leadership and the Exiles

easy.explanation: He captured Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah, the keepers of the door, and other officials.
easy.q: Whom did Nebuzar-adan capture among Judah’s leaders?

easy.explanation: They were brought to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
easy.q: Where were the captured leaders taken?

answers: They were smitten and put to death
easy.explanation: The king of Babylon smote them and put them to death in Riblah.
easy.q: What happened to the captured leaders at Riblah?

medium.explanation: Verse 25 mentions an eunuch who had charge of the men of war.
medium.q: Who was captured as having charge of the men of war?

answers: The one who mustered the people of the land
The one who guarded the Temple
medium.explanation: The principal scribe of the host mustered the people of the land.
medium.q: Who was the principal scribe of the host?

medium.explanation: The passage lists deportations in the seventh, eighteenth, and three-and-twentieth years.
medium.q: How many stages of deportation are listed?

challenge.explanation: The list shows that religious, military, administrative, and royal leaders were taken.
challenge.q: What does the list of priests, officials, and royal associates show?

answers: Three thousand and three and twenty
challenge.explanation: The seventh-year deportation included three thousand and three and twenty Jews.
challenge.q: How many Jews were carried away in the seventh year of Nebuchadrezzar?

challenge.explanation: Nebuzar-adan carried away seven hundred forty and five persons in that year.
challenge.q: How many persons were carried away in the three-and-twentieth year?

paragraphs.title: Jehoiachin’s Release and a Glimmer of Hope

easy.explanation: Evil-merodach king of Babylon brought Jehoiachin out of prison.

answers: He gave him an honored throne above other kings
He sent an army to Jerusalem
He gave him the city walls
easy.explanation: He set Jehoiachin’s throne above the throne of the kings with him in Babylon.
easy.q: What did Evil-merodach do for Jehoiachin?

easy.explanation: Jehoiachin continually ate bread before the king all the days of his life.

medium.explanation: The king changed Jehoiachin’s prison garments.
medium.q: What did Evil-merodach do with Jehoiachin’s prison garments?

medium.explanation: A continual diet was given to him every day.
medium.q: How often was Jehoiachin given a portion of food?

answers: He sent him into exile again
medium.explanation: The passage says that Evil-merodach spoke kindly unto him.

answers: A sign of renewed honor and hope
The end of every exile in Judah
challenge.explanation: His release, new clothing, honored throne, and daily food suggest renewed favor and hope.

answers: He received continual care and honor
challenge.explanation: The king provided Jehoiachin a regular portion every day for the rest of his life.
challenge.q: What does his daily food indicate about his new condition?

answers: Zedekiah was punished, while Jehoiachin was honored
Both were released at the same time
Both received daily food in Babylon
challenge.explanation: Zedekiah was blinded and imprisoned, while Jehoiachin was released and treated with favor.
challenge.q: What major contrast appears between Zedekiah and Jehoiachin?
